## Hi — I'm Stephen.

I've spent **20+ years** in bioinformatics, genomics, and life-sciences data science — which sounds like a long time until you realise how much the field has changed in just the last five. The questions have stayed the same though: **how do we make sense of complex biomedical data, and how do we turn it into something that actually helps people?**

At **[Biorelate](https://www.biorelate.com)** I lead Professional Services. In practice that means making sure the science we're doing connects to the problems our clients actually need solving — accelerating a drug-discovery pipeline, untangling a messy real-world data workflow, or helping a team understand what they've got and what they can do with it.

Before this I worked across **academia, the NHS, and pharma** — building and leading teams, shipping ML models, and trying to make large-scale data projects land well in the real world.

Oh, and somewhere along the way I appear to have become an **Agentic Engineer**. Not by design — more by osmosis and a stubborn refusal to fall behind the LLM Joneses. Right now I'm particularly interested in where **knowledge graphs, RAG, and multi-omics data** are heading, and what that means for personalised medicine.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Always happy to connect** with people working at the intersection of data, biology, and drug discovery. → [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sjnewhouse/) · [Email](mailto:stephen.j.newhouse@gmail.com)
:::

### What I'm working on

- **Biomedical AI at Biorelate** — knowledge graphs, NLP, target/drug/biomarker discovery, indication expansion.
- **Agentic AI** — memory, tool-use, evaluation. See [`aa-ma-forge`](https://github.com/snewhouse/aa-ma-forge).
- **Genomics tooling** — curating [`awesome-genetics-software`](https://github.com/snewhouse/awesome-genetics-software).
- **Writing & sharing** — see the [blog](posts.qmd) and [archived talks](archive.qmd).
